asgard.sub: The golden realm · one of the Nine Realms
asgard.d: The golden realm of the Norse gods, one of the Nine Realms — linked to Earth by the Bifröst. Went down in Ragnarök (planned by Thor to stop Hela); the survivors founded New Asgard in Norway, ruled today by Valkyrie.

wakanda.d: The most technologically advanced nation on Earth, disguised for centuries as a developing country. Its wealth: the vibranium meteorite. Home of the Black Panther line, the Dora Milaje and the heart-shaped-herb tradition.

kamartaj.sub: Home of the Masters of the Mystic Arts
kamartaj.d: Hidden monastery in Kathmandu, training ground of the Masters of the Mystic Arts and seat of the Sorcerer Supreme (currently: Wong). From here the three Sanctums in New York, London and Hong Kong are coordinated, magically shielding the Earth.

knowhere.sub: The head of the dead Celestial
knowhere.d: A mining station inside the severed head of a dead Celestial — black market, refuge and seat of the Collector, who archives everything remarkable in the universe there. Taken over by the Guardians after Thanos' attack and their home base today.

sakaar.d: Garbage planet at the edge of the universe, ringed by wormholes, ruled by the Grandmaster and his gladiator games. Here Thor became the 'Lord of Thunder' and Hulk spent two years as champion.

talokan.d: Underwater realm of a Maya people who fled into the sea from the conquistadors — the world's second vibranium power beside Wakanda. Ruled by the god-king K'uk'ulkan, whom the surface world calls Namor.

attilan.sub: The hidden city of the Inhumans
attilan.d: The hidden city of the Inhumans — located on the Moon in the series. Quietly buried after the Inhumans debacle; Black Bolt returned only as an Earth-838 variant.

kunlun.sub: The city of the Iron Fist
kunlun.d: Mystical city in another dimension that only periodically opens to Earth — training ground of the Iron Fist and home of the immortal dragon Shou-Lao.

genosha.d: The island state that was meant to be a home for mutants. In X-Men '97 the setting of the most devastating episode in Marvel animation ('Remember It') — a name that sets off alarm bells for X-Men fans.

xandar.d: Homeworld of the Nova Corps, the space police that guarded the Power Stone. Was devastated by Thanos between films — the Nova Corps is still waiting for its big-screen return.

titan.d: Thanos' ruined homeworld — a wreck that shaped his worldview: overpopulation destroyed it, so he wants to 'balance' the universe. Setting of the battle in which Doctor Strange gave up the Time Stone.

vormir.sub: Resting place of the Soul Stone
vormir.d: Desolate planet at the edge of the universe, resting place of the Soul Stone — guarded by Red Skull as a cursed ferryman. The stone demands a sacrifice: a soul you love. Gamora and Natasha died here.

nidavellir.d: Forge world of the dwarves around a neutron star — origin of Mjölnir, Stormbreaker and the Infinity Gauntlet. After Thanos' visit, Eitri is the last of his people.

quantenreich.d: Subatomic world outside time and space — Janet van Dyne's 30-year exile, Kang's prison and the key to Endgame's time travel. Enter only with Pym Particles.

void-ort.sub: The dump at the end of time
void-ort.d: The dump at the end of time: everything the TVA prunes from the timelines lands here — guarded by the cloud monster Alioth. Home of Cassandra Nova and final stop for countless Fox figures, until Deadpool came by.

newyork-sanctum.d: 177A Bleecker Street, Greenwich Village: one of Earth's three magical protection nodes and Strange's residence. For a sorcerer's household, astonishingly often demolished. Yes: this website is named after it.

avengers-tower.d: First Stark's tower in Manhattan (Avengers base from the Battle of New York on), then the Compound in upstate New York — destroyed in the Endgame finale in 2023. The tower sale was a fan riddle for years: the buyer was never revealed.

latveria-lex.d: Small Eastern European state under Doctor Doom's absolute rule: no poverty, no crime, no freedom. As a sovereign state, Latveria makes its ruler diplomatically untouchable — perhaps Doom's mightiest weapon.

battleworld-lex.sub: The patchwork world of Secret Wars
battleworld-lex.d: The patchwork planet built from the wreckage of dead universes, which Doom rules as God Emperor in the Secret Wars comics. By everything structure and comics suggest: the stage of Avengers: Secret Wars.

skrulle.d: Shapeshifting aliens whose homeworld the Kree destroyed. In the MCU first refugees (Captain Marvel), then infiltrators (Secret Invasion) — anyone can be a Skrull, which Marvel has used for several retcons.

kree.d: Warlike empire of blue-skinned aliens, ruled by the AI 'Supreme Intelligence'. Responsible for Carol's brainwashing, Ronan's fanaticism and the experiments that created the Inhumans.

chitauri.d: Thanos' rental army for the Battle of New York — cybernetic swarm beings controlled by a mothership. Their collapse after Tony's nuclear flight through the portal ended the invasion instantly.

celestials-lex.d: Cosmic titans who seed galaxies: their embryos gestate inside planetary cores and consume the world at birth. Ego was one, Tiamut was stopped by the Eternals — his frozen body is an adamantium mine today, and Knowhere sits in the skull of a third.

eternals-volk.d: Synthetic immortals created by the Celestials as a protector facade — their true mission: let humanity ripen as a Celestial incubator. The Deviants are their failed predecessor attempt.

asgardier.d: Long-lived (not immortal) warrior culture, worshipped by humans as gods. Decimated to a few thousand after Ragnarök and Thanos' raid — today a fishing village with a tourist attraction in Norway.

inhumans-volk.d: Humans altered by Kree experiments, whose powers awaken through Terrigen Mist. Kamala's series hinted her genes are Inhuman — the big Inhumans project itself crashed spectacularly in 2017.

mutanten.d: Humans with the X-gene, whose powers usually awaken in puberty. A Fox exclusive for two decades — they trickle into the MCU drop by drop: Kamala's 'mutation', Namor, Beast's cameo, and with Doomsday the dam breaks.

symbionten-lex.d: Alien liquid beings that amplify and influence hosts — Venom, Carnage and colleagues. Their creator Knull was teased in Venom 3; a symbiote remnant has been lying unnoticed in Earth-616 since No Way Home.

flerken-lex.d: Looks like a house cat, but harbors pocket dimensions full of tentacles in its mouth. Goose swallowed the Tesseract and scratched out Nick Fury's eye — the official truth behind the eyepatch.

watcher-volk.d: Ancient observers who catalogue every universe but may never intervene. Uatu narrates What If…? and broke his oath exactly once. Stan Lee's cameos are canonically their informant.

shield.d: The intelligence agency that gathered the heroes — founded by Peggy Carter and Howard Stark, led by Nick Fury. Collapsed in 2014 when it turned out: Hydra had lived on inside its walls since 1945.

hydra-lex.d: Red Skull's World War II science cult that took over S.H.I.E.L.D. from the inside ('Hail Hydra'). Creator of the Winter Soldier; officially crushed — a stretchy term with Hydra: cut off one head …

saber.d: The space successors of S.H.I.E.L.D.: S.W.O.R.D. rebuilt White Vision (WandaVision), S.A.B.E.R. is Fury's orbital station, where he has holed up since Secret Invasion.

tenrings-org.d: Wenwu's thousand-year shadow empire, named after his artifacts — long veiled in the MCU as the 'Mandarin myth' (Iron Man 3 says hello). Today led by Xialing, contrary to her announcement to dissolve it.

damagecontrol.d: The agency that cleans up after superhero battles — and grows increasingly heavy-handed: it indirectly created the Vulture, hunted Kamala and now locks up superhumans.

oscorp.d: Norman Osborn's corporation — the origin of evil in every Spider-Man world: Goblin serum, mutated spiders, Electro. Exists in the Raimi, Amazing and animated universes; hasn't (yet) appeared in the MCU.

starkindustries.d: From arms manufacturer to clean-tech giant: Howard's legacy, Tony's playground, Pepper's company. Supplied the MCU with everything from arc reactors to the AI family J.A.R.V.I.S./FRIDAY/E.D.I.T.H.

pymtech.d: Hank Pym's company and keeper of the Pym Particles — whose attempted thefts drive two whole Ant-Man films. Relaunched as the Pym van Dyne Foundation after Darren Cross's fall.

roxxon.d: The oil-and-everything conglomerate that keeps popping up as a background villain since Iron Man — Marvel's running gag for ruthless capitalism, most recently prominent in Loki as Victor Timely's adversary backdrop.

hand.d: Ancient ninja cult chasing immortality, puppet master of the Netflix era — enemy of Daredevil, resurrector of Elektra and the reason the Defenders ever met.

weaponx.d: The black project that coated Logan's skeleton with adamantium and mutilated Wade Wilson into Deadpool. In the Fox universe the name stands for everything done to mutants in labs.

essex.d: The name behind the Apocalypse post-credit scene: collector of mutant DNA, comics link to Mister Sinister — a Fox thread that was never paid off. In the multiverse, nothing is ever truly gone.

tva-lex.sub: The agency at the end of time
tva-lex.d: The agency at the end of time: formerly enforcer of the Sacred Timeline (with prune staffs and retro offices), after Loki's sacrifice disaster control for the sprawling multiverse. Most recently recruited Deadpool — their biggest mistake or stroke of genius.

ravagers-lex.sub: Pirates with a code of honor
ravagers-lex.d: Space privateers in a hundred feuding factions, united only by the code. Yondu's clan raised Peter Quill; his funeral with the assembled fleet is one of the most beautiful moments of the series.

snap-lex.d: 2018: Thanos snaps with all six stones and erases half of all life in the universe. The world stayed halved for five years — the most formative event in MCU history.

blip-lex.d: 2023: Hulk's counter-snap brings everyone who vanished back — exactly where and as old as when they disappeared. The chaos afterwards (lost apartments, doubled lives, refugee crises) occupies series and films to this day.

schlacht-ny.d: 2012: Loki opens the Chitauri portal over Manhattan, six heroes become the Avengers. For the MCU the big bang of the superhero era — and via the Endgame time heist also the birth of the Loki variant.

sokovia-lex.d: In 2015 Ultron lifts a city into the sky; in 2016 the world answers with the Sokovia Accords for hero oversight — the rift that splits the Avengers in Civil War. Later quietly buried; the distrust remained.

westview.d: Wanda wraps a small town in a sitcom reality and holds thousands of residents captive as involuntary extras. 'The Hex' introduced the world to chaos magic — and made Wanda the most feared person on the planet.

multiversalkrieg.d: The primordial war in which Kang variants fought each other with entire timelines — ended by He Who Remains with the brutal solution: a single permitted timeline. At its core, Doomsday is the looming round two.

vergessen.d: 2024: to save the multiverse, Doctor Strange makes the whole world forget that Peter Parker exists. The highest price any MCU hero has ever paid — Brand New Day shows the life after.

voidtag.d: 2026: Sentry's dark self swallows parts of New York into shadow until Yelena's team reaches him inside his trauma. Afterwards Valentina markets the crew as the 'New Avengers' — the current state of the hero world.

kanon-ereignis-lex.d: Spider-Verse concept: key moments (the bite, the captain's death) that must happen in every Spider story or the universe collapses — says Miguel O'Hara. Miles Morales is the living objection.

incursion-lex.d: The collision of two universes that erases one or both — triggered by too many border violations between worlds. The technical term driving Doomsday and Secret Wars; we have already seen one.

ragnarok-lex.d: Asgard's prophesied twilight of the gods — deliberately triggered by Thor (Surtur freed, crown into the Eternal Flame) to bury Hela with the realm. Proof that you can fulfill a prophecy in order to win.

vibranium-lex.d: Meteorite metal that absorbs and stores energy — the basis of Wakanda's technology, Cap's shield and Talokan's reefs. The most coveted material on Earth, and with Doomsday more than ever.

adamantium-lex.d: The practically indestructible metal on Wolverine's bones — officially in the MCU since Brave New World: mined from the dead Celestial in the Indian Ocean. A raw material with a built-in X-Men announcement.

serum.d: Dr. Erskine's formula that created Steve Rogers — and whose imitations produced almost only monsters: Red Skull, Abomination, the Flag Smashers, John Walker. The serum amplifies what is inside a person. That is exactly the problem.

extremis.d: Killian's bio-upgrade from Iron Man 3: regenerates limbs, makes skin glow hot — and occasionally makes test subjects explosive. Never mentioned again, although it would have revolutionized half of Marvel science.

pym-lex.d: Particles that change the distance between atoms: shrink, grow, Quantum Realm. Strictly guarded by Hank Pym — and the only fuel that makes Endgame's time travel work.

terrigen.d: The Kree process that activates dormant Inhuman genes — classically via Terrigen Mist. Kamala's bangle triggered something similar in her; the series then called her gene a 'mutation'. Marvel keeps every door open.

chaosmagie.d: The oldest, rawest form of magic: not bending reality but rewriting it. The Darkhold prophesies the Scarlet Witch as its bearer — mightier than any Sorcerer Supreme.

powercosmic.d: The primal force of the Celestials and Galactus — granted to his heralds like the Silver Surfer: reshape matter, channel energy, travel between worlds. The top league of cosmic powers.

phoenix.d: Cosmic primal force that seeks out hosts like Jean Grey — filmed twice by Fox, twice it consumed its bearer. One of the few powers even Apocalypse respected.

heilfaktor.d: Cell regeneration at absurd levels: Wolverine grows back, Deadpool is practically immortal (and cancer-ridden at the same time — his curse). Also explains Logan's age of almost 200 years.

anker-lex.d: A person on whose existence the stability of their entire universe hangs — if they die, the world slowly dies with them. Logan was the anchor of the Fox universe; who the MCU's is has never been revealed. Unsettling.

variante-lex.d: Any alternative version of a person from another timeline — from alligator Loki to Kang's thousand conquerors. The central question before Doomsday: is Doom a variant of someone we know?

heilige-zeitlinie-lex.d: The one permitted timeline that He Who Remains left after the Multiversal War, guarded by the TVA. History since Sylvie's sword thrust — today Loki holds the free branches together with his own hands.

nexus-lex.d: Individuals who can massively influence timelines — Wanda and Loki are among them. The WandaVision commercial 'Nexus' was the hidden hint, long before Loki explained it.

darkhold-lex.d: Chthon's Book of the Damned: promises power, corrupts every reader. Wanda's fall in Multiverse of Madness bears its signature — in the end she destroyed every copy in every universe.

jarvis.d: Tony's AI dynasty: J.A.R.V.I.S. (later Vision's foundation), FRIDAY, E.D.I.T.H. — and Ultron as the black sheep. The question of whether Stark's AIs are persons was answered by Vision with his existence.

stanlee-lex.d: The creator of the Marvel universe appeared in almost every film — as driver, general, Watcher informant. Guardians Vol. 2 made it canon: all his appearances are ONE character. The complete list is in the records.

postcredits-lex.d: Marvel's invention as a storytelling tool: since Nick Fury's 'Avenger Initiative' (2008), staying seated pays off. Rules of thumb: mid-credit = plot, post-credit = joke or tease. The complete chain is in the paths.

fsk-lex.d: MCU films and Disney+ series are canon; the Netflix era is a gray zone (Cox, D'Onofrio and Bernthal were carried over, the rest floats); Fox and Sony are their own universes — but since the multiverse officially part of the same reality-of-realities. In short: more counts than Marvel used to admit.
